messages:
Alex: Heads up — ran a targeted recompute for yesterday's EU hourly aggregates and saw a 3x spike in CPU / I/O on the reprocess fleet. Console shows a big cost blip. anyone else see this?
Maya: Noted, can you paste the job id and the API call you used?
Alex: Job id: recompute-eu-171820. API call:
```
POST /api/v1/recompute
{
  "scope": "eu:hourly:2026-03-20",
  "mode": "targeted",
  "priority": "normal"
}
```
Priya: Hmm, normal priority on EU during morning window might have overlapped with snapshot garbage collection. Did the job pick dedicated vs hosted routing?
Alex: It hit hosted first, then fell back to dedicated nodes after queue pressure. The routing trace shows `routing_hint: null`.
Sam: This screams for a routing-safe-mode in the console. We should let ops flip a bakeoff that prefers low-cost quantized model variants for reprocesses and routes traffic off latency-critical pools.
Dinesh: Agreed. Also reclaiming cache keys during recompute is causing KV cache churn for live requests — noticed higher tail latency on hosts serving live traffic.
Maya: Can we avoid cache invalidation by running recompute with `cache_isolation: true`? Is that exposed in the internal API?
Priya: There's an internal param `quiet_write=true` on the rehydrate endpoint but it's not exposed in the self-serve console. If we set `quiet_write` + `prefer_quantized` + `slot_quota=0.05` we could limit blast radius.
Alex: Example payload I tried locally:
```
POST /api/v1/recompute
{
  "scope": "eu:hourly:2026-03-20",
  "mode": "targeted",
  "priority": "low",
  "routing_hint": "prefer_low_cost",
  "quiet_write": true,
  "slot_quota": 0.05
}
```
Sam: We should debate whether `routing_hint` belongs in the public internal API or only in the operator CLI. If app teams can set it, they might unintentionally route away from SLA-backed pools.
Maya: Proposal: expose `routing_hint` in console behind an enterprise feature flag and add guardrails: UI warns about SLA impact, default to disabled for hosted customers.
Dinesh: We'll also need runtime checks to prevent a recompute from draining all dedicated slots — quota enforcement is necessary. `slot_quota` param looks good but needs validation server-side.
Priya: From an observability standpoint, console should show a per-job breakdown: routed model variant, slots consumed, peak CPU, cache invalidation rate. Right now the job page only shows start/finish + bytes processed.
Alex: +1 on observability. I had to jump to infra logs to see the fallback to dedicated. Not discoverable in the console.
Sam: I'll mock a small UX change: add a `Safe Recompute` toggle on the job creation modal that sets `routing_hint=prefer_low_cost`, `quiet_write=true`, and `slot_quota=0.05`. It will surface warnings about quality regressions.
Maya: I'll open an RFC to add the `routing_hint` / `quiet_write` / `slot_quota` params to the internal recompute API and add server-side validators to enforce min/max quotas per-tenant. Tagging @Dinesh for runtime validation and @Sam for console.
Dinesh: I'll add a runtime guard to reject `slot_quota` < 0.01 or > 0.5 and will add a safety circuit that prechecks current dedicated slot usage before scheduling.
Priya: Also request: surface a small quicklink from the job page to the affected aggregates in the dashboard so product owners can eyeball potential quality delta.
Alex: Thanks. For now I re-ran the target with `priority: low` + `slot_quota: 0.02` and it completed with much smaller impact. Posting short summary to the incident slack channel. :thumbsup:
replay-bot: reprocess-job recompute-eu-171820 transitioned -> COMPLETED (runtime 00:45:12, peak_slots=12)
Maya: Perfect. RFC link: tinyurl.com/rfc-recompute-routing (I will update with PRs).
Sam: I'll drop a minimal console PR and feature flag. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Dinesh: Runtime change will be a small API validator + precheck. I'll put up a draft branch.
Priya: Great — once we have the console toggle and validators we can run a controlled bakeoff next week and measure cost/quality deltas.
Alex: Sounds good. Thanks all.
